freshness_window.rationale: Canonical 14-day discover window per program spec. Frame's most-recent date_announced is 2026-05-12 (61 entities total), so the window picks up exactly where the existing corpus ends — no overlap waste, no gap.

params.query: company announces layoffs workforce reduction May 2026

queries.rationale: Broad semantic news sweep for company×layoff announcements in the 14-day window. Exa's neural news category is the highest-recall single query per dollar for discover.

params.query: WARN notice filing 8-K SEC workforce reduction layoffs

queries.rationale: Authoritative-filing slice — surfaces WARN Act notices and 8-K disclosures, which are the highest-tier sources for layoff_count and date_announced per the authoritative source rule.
Targets the dominant 2026 layoff reason enum value (ai-restructuring). Complements the broad sweep with a reason-stated semantic angle that often catches mid-size tech/AI cuts the broad query misses.

params.query: (layoffs OR "job cuts" OR "workforce reduction") -filter:retweets lang:en since:2026-05-12 until:2026-05-26

queries.rationale: First-party corroboration slice — CEO/company posts on X. Authority tier 2 (primary) when a CEO names a headcount. Date operators scope to the freshness window.

notes: All 4 queries use only chosen_tools (exa_search, twitter_search). 3 exa slices + 1 twitter slice = 4 distinct slices across 2 tools. Freshness window explicit in every query (exa via startPublishedDate/endPublishedDate, twitter via since:/until: operators). Headroom of $0.16 left under the $0.20 ceiling — caller can request additional slices (semantic-memo-style, semantic-ceo-statement) without exceeding budget if needed downstream.
